subjects.displayTitle: A channel for the spirit: humility, speech, and service
subjects.introduction: Be a channel for bounty, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá writes, and then raises the stakes: become bounty yourself. The teacher he describes is a reed through which the Holy Spirit may flow, a heart emptied of self that can start a fire in a cold one, a bird at dawn exhilarated by its own song. Attraction, zeal and severance from mortal things come first; eloquence and talent, he observes, have sometimes accomplished nothing while the tongue-tied prospered, because the real capital of a teacher is divine power rather than skill. The humility this asks is exacting. Preparation, courage in speaking and the willingness to act remain ours; another person’s response does not. Paul drew the same line when he called himself and Apollos servants who plant and water while God alone gives the growth [1]. A single soul may go forth and find legions behind it, provided the will is submissive and the speaker says what is cast into the heart. The way leads on to the Holy Spirit itself, to becoming a source of living waters, to the state of enkindlement, and to the confirmations promised to those who arise.
subjects.arc: Begin with becoming bounty, explore the inward qualities of a channel, move into courageous speech, and end with action, mutual trust, and the gift of life.

order.why: Name the inward qualities associated with guidance.
shortened: Guidance is due to the Power of the Holy Spirit. He who wishes to become a teacher, must first instill in his own heart the attributes thus mentioned, namely: attraction, zeal and severance from attachments to mortal things. Then will he be astounded by the forthcoming results.

order.why: Open with the memorable movement from channeling bounty to becoming bounty.
shortened: Be a channel for bounty, nay rather become yourself true bounty.

order.why: Consider the teacher’s own renewal through the image of a singing bird.
shortened: However, when the tongue of the teacher is engaged in teaching, he will naturally himself be stimulated, will become a magnet attracting the divine aid and bounty of the Kingdom, and will be like unto the bird at the hour of dawn, which itself becometh exhilarated by its own singing, its warbling and its melody....

order.why: Read the image of a heart emptied of self and able to kindle warmth.
shortened: If he be entirely detached and emptied of self he will be enabled to start in a cold heart a great fire.

order.why: Consider spiritual companionship and confirmation.
Place the search for truth within the language of divine favor.
Read the invitation to strive toward inspiration.
shortened: Each one of you should strive with all your heart to become a manifestor of God's inspiration.

order.why: Explore the need to protect and sustain an inward flame.
shortened: Therefore my advice to you is: Become ye ignited with that Flame, be ye enkindled with that Fire! Never let the light of your spirit die out, protect it from the gales of the stormy nights, shield it from the raging tempest of the outside world and guard it from the turbulent hurricane of the wintry season.

order.why: Connect enkindlement with the relief of troubled hearts.
shortened: But it is essential that you should be enkindled by the breath of the Holy Spirit and with full firmness and perseverance you should enkindle the fire of the love of God in the heart, and with no more power over thy own will, you should unconsciously cry out and proclaim the appearance of the Kingdom of God, so that these troubled hearts may become free and conflicting thoughts may disappear and the candle of guidance may illumine them all.

order.why: Read the imagery of inspired speech and life-giving influence.
shortened: Whosoever is filled with the love of Baha and forgets all things - the Holy Spirit breathes into his mouth and the spirit of life into his heart, the lights of verses shine from his face, words scatter like strings of pearls from his mouth, and he heals ills and sickness by the touch of his hand.

order.why: Preserve the parallel supplied formulation.
Widen the image toward a world becoming a garden.
Identifies teaching as productive of the confirmations of the Holy Spirit and illumination of humanity.
Consider the spreading of teachings through spiritual influence.
shortened: Indeed thou wilt see the teachings of God spread in those regions by the breath of the Holy Spirit, and thou wilt discover the fragrances of the paradise of the Kingdom.

order.why: Read the encouragement to speak with confidence.
Develop the appeal to courageous speech in gatherings.
shortened: Rest ye assured that the Breathes of the Holy Spirit shall inspire you with the power of speech. Consequently loosen your tongues and speak in every meeting with undaunted courage.

order.why: Consider the attitude of a sincere worker facing questions.
shortened: A sincere worker in the Cause of God is always assisted by the Divine Spirit when such questions arise. The Truth will flow through you if you stand in the right attitude toward the Truth.

order.why: Read the brief assurance of aid beyond physical forces.
shortened: You are the conquerors, because the power of the Holy Spirit is your assistant. Above and over physical forces, phenomenal forces, the Holy Spirit itself shall aid you.

order.why: Examine the comparison with the early Christian teachers.
Read the reported contrast between eloquence and spiritual confirmation.
shortened: They went to America and were good speakers and had many talents. They knew English well. Nevertheless, they accomplished nothing, while we sent those who were dumb and the work progressed.

Now, wherever any of the friends of God may go, the hosts of divine confirmation will reach them. This is why Christ said to His disciples, "I am with you." Rest assured that the Holy Spirit will confirm you, and when you speak, do not think - say whatever is cast into your hearts.

order.why: Complete the linked readings with the third-hand report, retaining its stated mediation.
Preserve the concise emphasis on the teacher being affected.
shortened: The teacher, when teaching, must be himself fully enkindled, so that his utterance, like unto a flame of fire, may exert influence and consume the veil of self and passion.

order.why: Close with images of light and water offered to humanity.
shortened: You are the angels of Abha; guide the people. You are the rays of the Sun of Reality; bestow upon them light. You are the trees of the orchard of God; produce loving fruits, You are the water of eternal life; allay the thirst of mankind.

order.why: Read the reed-and-water image in its simplest form.
Explore learning and character development through the act of teaching.
Distinguish explaining the message from confirming a soul.
Connect influence with living the life being described.
Preserve the separately supplied formulation of those qualities.
Consider dedication as a condition of serving another person’s growth.
Connect prayer, reflection, and action.
shortened: The true basis of prayer is for the individual to hold himself as a reed, through which the Holy Spirit may flow. His will should be completely submissive to the Will of God. When this is done, then the Hosts of the Unseen Kingdom have an opportunity to assist and direct the individual.

The Guardian has so often pointed out that there are three elements of prayer -- meditation, supplication and action. It is most important that an individual act, because it is only while the individual is acting that a prayer can be answered.

order.why: Attend to gradual teaching and mutual confidence.
Return to the reed as an image of humility.

questions: What does it mean to become bounty oneself, beyond speaking about generosity?
How do the images of a reed, a flame, and a singing bird illuminate different aspects of service?
What responsibilities remain with the teacher if spiritual confirmation cannot be produced or claimed as a personal achievement?
How does Paul’s image of planting and watering illuminate cooperation and humility?
How might mutual trust, lived example, and willingness to learn help distinguish service from a desire to control another person’s response?

neighbors.invitation: Explore dedication through the qualities of a lived example.
Consider friendship when another person does not wish to pursue religious teaching.
Read about becoming more capable through the effort to serve.

references.label: 1 · 1 Corinthians 3:5–9 (King James Version)
references.note: Paul describes himself and Apollos as servants with different tasks: planting and watering, while growth is attributed to God. Compare that distinction with the reed through which spiritual influence flows. Both images leave room for real human labor while challenging the desire to claim another person’s faith as one’s own accomplishment.

subjects.displayTitle: Devotion in teaching: the gift of a life
subjects.introduction: Devotion shows in small arithmetic: how the hours of a day are spent, which comforts are let go, whose need is noticed first. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá writes to a husband and wife to consecrate their nights and days together to the Word of God, and to others that the sole object of a life should be its teaching. Such language is ardent, and it is meant to be. It speaks of forsaking rest, of sacrificing ambition, of crossing oceans to lands untouched by one’s ancestors, of people who bore persecution and counted it a gift. Yet the fire is never separated from sincerity, loyalty, and the living of the life, since knowledge without these kindles nothing. The Bhagavad-gītā’s counsel to do one’s duty without clinging to its fruits offers a kindred discipline of motive from another tradition [1]. To follow devotion further is to ask what spiritual prerequisites a teacher needs, where confidence and courage come from when the way is hard, and how zeal can be kept warm without burning the people it hopes to serve.
subjects.arc: Begin with shared and sincere service, consider the choices devotion entails, read the accounts of hardship, and return to character and daily acts of dedication.

order.why: Explore deliberate thought and planning about faithfulness.
Open with husband and wife serving together.
Place sincerity and purity of motive at the center of commitment.
Urges focused and sustained teaching, purity of character, support for devoted teachers and use of opportunities.
Read the joy occasioned by wholehearted service.
Consider the surrender of personal ambition.
shortened: Dedicate your lives to the service of the Beloved of Truth and sacrifice all your ambitions in the Path of the Merciful.

order.why: Read the strong expression of a life organized around teaching.
Consider the reported emphasis on service wherever one is.
Attend to the ardent call to speak and present proofs.
Read the challenge to sacrifice comfort.
shortened: We must sacrifice our comfort for Him; sacrifice all our conditions in the pathway of His service. If we do this, our service will be productive of great results. Otherwise God will raise up souls to do this work in our stead.

order.why: See that challenge expressed through journeys between communities.
shortened: Some of the friends of the All-Merciful have forsaken their physical comfort and ease, and have gone from city to city and village to village diffusing the divine fragrances.

order.why: Consider the fuller prayer for a traveler entering an unfamiliar land.
Read the recollection of giving both life and wealth.
Consider zeal in the language of eternal life.
shortened: Through his zeal, he will sacrifice everything in the path of God, and quaff from the chalice of eternal life.

order.why: Read the reported description of wholehearted self-sacrifice.
Remember the persecution endured in the promotion of the teachings.
shortened: The believers of God have accepted this Cause through self-sacrifice. They have given up their lives for it. They have accepted happily chains and fetters in order to promote these Teachings.

order.why: Preserve the language of the lover’s journey toward the Beloved.
Complete the linked readings with the comparison to Christ’s disciples.
Begin the additional selections with a shared pledge to bear hardship.
Read the account of leaving home and crossing oceans.
shortened: O thou daughter of the Kingdom! When his honor, Mr. Remey, returned to the Holy Land from his trip to China, Japan and India, and presented himself with the utmost glad tidings and happiness, he remembered the friends through absolute love and asked for them in the Threshold of Holiness, protection and providence from His Highness the One. Truly I say this beloved of Abduil Baha left his native land, turned his back upon the comforts and pleasures of home, accepted the difficulties of travel, and crossed the Pacific and the Atlantic Oceans.

order.why: Connect striving with conduct shaped by divine counsel.
shortened: O ye two lovers of the Beauty of ABHA! Ere long the Word of God will display a wonderful influence and finally that region (America) will become the paradise of ABHA. Consequently, strive ye bravely that this aim may be accomplished in the near future. Striving means this: Ye must live and move according to the divine commands and behests, be united in loving with ecstasy and joy; do not take any rest but engage continually in the service of the Cause of God.

order.why: Preserve the emphatic poetic language of unremitting effort.
Consider the relation between devotion and knowledge.
Explore the torch as an image of influence.
Read the connection of consecration and confirmation.
Return to the importance of living the life.
Consider devotion through its contribution to a recipient’s spiritual growth.
Close with daily attention to bringing life to a seeker.

questions: What ordinary decisions might reveal the difference between an admired ideal and a guiding commitment?
How do the accounts of travel and hardship deepen the meaning of devotion without making every person’s service take the same form?
What can the Bhagavad-gītā’s counsel about action without attachment contribute to reflection on motive and results?
How should knowledge, sincerity, and lived example strengthen one another in teaching?
How might a community interpret the collection’s ardent language of sacrifice in ways that sustain generous service and care for human life?

neighbors.invitation: Explore the humility and mutual trust involved in gradual teaching.
Consider joyful service amid an awareness of limitations.
Read the explicit command to preserve life in the path of service.

references.label: 1 · Bhagavad-gītā 3.19 (A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda translation, Bhaktivedanta Book Trust)
references.note: The verse joins the performance of duty with freedom from attachment to the fruits of action. Compare that discipline of motive with the selections on relinquishing ambition and giving oneself to service. The comparison concerns dedication and attachment; the verse belongs to its own religious account of duty and the supreme goal.

subjects.displayTitle: Exalting the Word: roots in the heart, fruit in the life
subjects.introduction: The Word of God, Bahá’u’lláh says, is a sapling whose roots have been planted in human hearts, and the task of the believer is to water it with wisdom and holy words until its branches reach the heavens. To exalt the Word, then, is less a matter of volume than of cultivation. It asks for study and meditation, for verses learned by heart so that the right one is ready when the occasion calls, for courage, whose very source is the promotion of the Word, and for endurance when the ills of the world press in. Above all it asks for a life that bears the words out: goodly deeds and a praiseworthy character are the hosts that attract hearts and unlock the gates of cities, and conduct can raise the banner of the Cause or lower it. Faithfulness to the text and freedom of expression belong together, since the truth is what the divine Lights have said while each person may find fresh ways to approach it. Isaiah pictures the word as rain and snow that do not return to heaven until the earth has brought forth seed and bread [1]. The path leads on to the methods of teaching the Cause and to the influence and centrality of the Word itself.
subjects.arc: Begin with the growing sapling, develop study and a credible life, then explore perseverance, faithful explanation, and the wisdom of offering words at the right time.

order.why: Open with the sapling rooted in human hearts.
Connect nourishment with study, meditation, and remembered passages.
Call attention to wisdom as a companion of utterance.
Consider the way conduct can raise or lower a cause.
Read the hoped-for effects on disturbed and dispirited people.
shortened: Today one must engage in exalting the Word of God by whatever means, so that the veiled may awaken, the disturbed may find peace and stability, the dispirited may become enkindled, and the lifeless may be stirred to motion.

order.why: Connect exaltation of the Word with illumination of human life.
shortened: You had no desire except for the illumination of the human world and no point of focus except the exaltation of the Word of God and the spread of the heavenly teachings.

order.why: Read the source of courage in steadfast promotion.
shortened:
The source of courage and power is the promotion of
the Word of God, and steadfastness in His Love.

order.why: Develop the theme of constancy.
Read the prayer for strength through tribulation.
shortened: I implore Thee to assist me and them that love me to magnify Thy Word, and to endow us with such strength that the ills of this world and its tribulations will be powerless to hinder us from remembering Thee and from extolling Thy virtues.

order.why: Recognize endeavor according to capacity.
shortened: That soul must at all times exert their utmost endeavor, according to their capacity, in the exaltation of the Word of God.

order.why: Consider the attention and effort required.
shortened: A world of striving is needed, and a world of attention, that the standard of the Most Great Word may be raised aloft upon the flags.

order.why: Read the appeal to make proofs widely known.
Pause over the concise call of the present day.
shortened: O spiritual friends! Today is the day of exalting the Word of God.

order.why: Consider the gathering of people in shared endeavor.
shortened: From all directions they hasten beneath the shadow of the banner of divine favors and strive to exalt the Word of God.

order.why: Read the connection with self-sacrifice.
Examine actions in relation to the honor of religion.
Attend to the counsel concerning reverence and conduct.
Complete the linked readings with a brief prayer for aid.
Directly urges teaching, exalting the Word of God and diffusing divine fragrances.
Begin the additional selections with the image of new doors opening through repeated reading.
Connect words with the influence of deeds and character.
shortened: In these days, in one of the Tablets, this exalted word hath flowed from the Most Exalted Pen -- glorified be His utterance: "At all times, hold fast to that which will cause the exaltation of the Word of God. Goodly deeds and a praiseworthy character are the hosts of God in this supreme Revelation, and likewise are blessed and goodly words. These hosts attract hearts and unlock the gates of cities. This weapon is sharper than the weapons of the world."

order.why: Consider the discernment that sometimes calls for silence.
shortened: Arise thou to serve the Cause of thy Lord; then give the people the joyful tidings concerning this resplendent Light whose revelation hath been announced by God through His Prophets and Messengers. Admonish everyone moreover to observe prudence as ordained by Him, and in the Name of God advise them, saying: It behooveth every one in this Day of God to dedicate himself to the teaching of the Cause with utmost prudence and steadfastness. Should he discover a pure soil, let him sow the seed of the Word of God, otherwise it would be preferable to observe silence.

order.why: Read the assurance of support after the departure of the Manifestation.
shortened: Be not dismayed, O peoples of the world, when the day-star of My beauty is set, and the heaven of My tabernacle is concealed from your eyes. Arise to further My Cause, and to exalt My Word amongst men. We are with you at all times, and shall strengthen you through the power of truth.

order.why: Close with a prayer for truth and the dawning of light in hearts.
shortened: O my God, aid Thou Thy servant to raise up the Word, and to refute what is vain and false, to establish the truth, to spread the sacred verses abroad, reveal the splendors, and make the morning's light to dawn in the hearts of the righteous.

order.why: Distinguish authoritative words from individual explanation while preserving freedom of expression.
shortened: Surely the ideal way of teaching is to prove our points by constant reference to the actual words of Baha'u'llah and the Master. This will save the Cause from being misinterpreted by individuals. It is what these divine Lights say that is truth and therefore they should be the authorities of our statements. This, however, does not mean that our freedom of expression is limited. We can always find new ways of approach to that truth or explain how they influence our life and condition.

order.why: Read the further insistence on returning to the Word itself.
Preserve the direct appeal to share sacred words.
Return to the central aspiration of heedful souls.

questions: What changes when teaching is imagined as watering a sapling rather than simply transmitting information?
How do good deeds and character give credibility to the words a person shares?
What is the relationship between faithful reference to a sacred text and the freedom to find a fresh way of explaining its meaning?
How does Isaiah’s image of rain enrich the compilation’s account of the Word’s influence?
What might help a person discern when to speak, when to listen, and when to leave space for another’s reflection?

neighbors.invitation: Read the cupbearer’s attention to whether anyone seeks the cup.
Consider the relationship between knowledge and devotion.
Explore the teacher’s own learning through the act of teaching.

references.label: 1 · Isaiah 55:10–11 (Hebrew–English text, Mechon Mamre)
references.note: Isaiah compares the divine word with rain and snow that water the earth, enabling seed and food to grow. Compare this with the sapling rooted in the heart and the call to nourish it with wisdom. Consider both the confidence in the word’s purpose and the human responsibility to cultivate conditions for understanding.

subjects.displayTitle: Few receptive souls: patience, grace, and the work of seeking
subjects.introduction: Many are thirsty, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá observes, but very few serve as cupbearers. The remark turns an old complaint on its head: the shortage that grieves him most is not of listeners but of those willing to carry the cup, and the cry for teachers rises from every direction. He is candid that true recognition is rare, that learned men have passed by what children of the Kingdom received, that believers are scarcer than red sulphur and steadfast love rarer still. What keeps this from curdling into self-importance is his insistence that guidance is a grace and not a reward: many are called, and the few who are chosen have nothing to boast of. Fewness, moreover, has a strange power; a handful of believers in the days of Christ overcame multitudes, and the few violets of a Baghdad courtyard were dearer than a field of them. Mark’s parable of seed on the path, among stones, in thorns and on good ground [1] asks the same questions about reception and eventual fruit. Those who left under tests later returned, so no one’s response is fixed. The road runs on to the saying that many are called but few are chosen, to the receptivity of the hearer, and to the methods of teaching.
subjects.arc: Begin with the scarcity of cupbearers, place recognition within grace, explore the influence of small beginnings, and then consider the recurring images of an abundant gift awaiting a hearing.

order.why: Consider the far-reaching influence attributed to a small number of believers.
shortened: Though but few persons accepted and were converted in the Day of each one of the Manifestations, yet these few surpassed and overcame great multitudes. During the time of Christ only a few souls believed in Him, but they were so powerful in spirit that none of the learned men among the Israelites could resist and stand against them, and afterward their light illumined the world, their call was raised abroad, their stars twinkled in heaven, their diadem became resplendent, and they are shining with great brilliancy.

order.why: Place guidance within grace rather than personal worthiness.
shortened: O ye who are attracted to the Beauty of Truth! Christ - may my soul be a sacrifice unto Him - hath said in the Gospel: "Many are called but few are chosen." This meaneth that while many are invited to the Faith, few are those who attain to the grace of guidance and the succour of divine favour, for the gift of guidance is purely an outpouring of grace and bounty, not dependent on capacity and worthiness.

order.why: Open by shifting attention from a lack of listeners to a lack of cupbearers.
shortened: In these days there are many who thirst but very few who serve as cupbearers.

order.why: Read the urgent cry for teachers.
Imagine those who remain to tend a garden.
Consider the contrast between learning and recognition.
shortened: Praise be to God that through His preceding mercy, His all-encompassing grace, and His all-pervading favors, thou hast attained recognition of the Dawning-Place of God's verses and the Dayspring of divine revelation. How many among the learned remained deprived of this supreme gift, while thou hast attained unto it!

order.why: Read the image of children receiving what sages miss.
Examine the reported comparison with recognition of Christ.
shortened: The bats do not perceive the light of the sun and the beetles cannot enjoy the fragrances of a rose-garden.

Consider that the horizons of the world were enlightened through the light of the Beauty of His Holiness Christ; yet all the people were asleep, blind and sightless, except a few whose eyes were opened and perceived the lights.

order.why: Read the contrast between fewness and abundance.
Explore the violet image used to express the value of rare beginnings.
Notice that those who departed under tests could later return.
shortened: In those days the tests were so great that out of three hundred and fifty believers only a handful remained but later on they returned.

order.why: Acknowledge different responses to the same call.
shortened: How many a servant hath heard the call and turned away therefrom, and how many a servant hath heard and was attracted by the verses of his Lord.

order.why: Read the image of a divine book addressing the earth.
Consider bounty overflowing despite limited reception.
Read the spiritual feast awaiting those who seek it.
Explore the paired images of fragrant roses and flowing knowledge.
shortened: The fragrances of the roses of inner meanings were diffused and the waters of knowledge were flowing, yet few were the seekers.

order.why: Consider wisdom as a treasure lacking a buyer.
shortened: Today there are seekers for all things except the pearls of wisdom and utterance that have appeared from the treasury of the Most Exalted Pen. These remain without seeker or buyer.

order.why: Read the lament over few who draw near.
shortened: Yet I find none possessed of hearing to hearken unto them and turn towards them and draw nigh through them, save a few numbered souls.

order.why: Distinguish having heard from being moved.
shortened: Souls are many who in the years gone by have listened to the glad-tidings, but up to this time they have remained veiled, deprived and unmoved.

order.why: Attend to the difference between tasting and drinking.
Read the purposes assigned to tongue and eyes.
Preserve the concise statement about an unaccepted gift.
Consider the renewed voice of Sinai.
shortened: Yet when the Sun of Revelation dawned from the horizon of the world, and the Speaker of Sinai spoke forth, all were found to be veiled save a few.

order.why: Read the contrast between prolonged speculation and response to a present call.
Preserve the further reference to the primordial covenant.
shortened: For the covenant of "Am I not your Lord?" was well known and universal, and yet all forgot it, save for a handful of souls more scarce than the philosopher's stone.

order.why: Return to the image of receptive hearing.
shortened: However, as pure and receptive ears are rare, therefore but few souls have attained and turned towards the Most Exalted Horizon.

order.why: Links the scarcity of hearing ears with the call to good deeds, praiseworthy character and fear of God.
Consider the reported rarity of discernment across ages.
shortened: Discerning, conscious souls, who comprehend the Reality of the Divine teachings are few in every age...

order.why: Read the first image of believers as rarer than red sulphur.
shortened: Nevertheless, when the veils were rent asunder, and the clouds were lifted, and the Countenance of the Intended One appeared and was made manifest from the horizon of the heaven of revelation, all arose in opposition and protest, though all were expectant. This is why He formerly said that true believers are rarer than red sulphur.

order.why: Preserve its separately supplied parallel.
shortened: The believer in God has always been and will continue to be rarer than red sulfur.

order.why: Complete the linked readings with steadfast love as the rare quality.
shortened: By your life, in this age those who are steadfast in love are rarer than the greatest elixir.

order.why: Close the selections with the Báb’s statement in its own attribution and religious setting.
shortened: Do ye feel secure against God's Self, the Most High, finding in truth a place of return? God hath made manifest thy signs to the peoples of earth and heaven, all together through the Gate. None believe in God and His signs in truth save a few of the foremost believers among the people of the Gate. Most people have been decreed by the All-Merciful's leave to be among those who join partners with their True Lord. None believe in God and His pure Remembrance save very few of the earliest ones.

questions: How does the opening image of too few cupbearers change the way we understand apparent scarcity?
What might the description of guidance as grace imply for how believers regard themselves and those who do not share their faith?
How does the parable of the sower illuminate differences between an initial response and lasting fruitfulness?
What can small beginnings accomplish that a simple count of adherents would fail to reveal?
How can the report of people later returning encourage patience and caution about treating receptivity as a fixed personal trait?

neighbors.invitation: Consider the warning against assuming we can judge the extent of another person’s receptivity.
Read the encouragement to persevere when results are slow.
Explore patient relationships founded on mutual confidence.

references.label: 1 · Mark 4:3–9 (King James Version)
references.note: The parable follows seed falling on a path, stony ground, among thorns, and on good ground, where it bears differing yields. Compare the attention to reception and fruitfulness with this compilation’s images of hearing, tasting, and tending a garden. The analogy can prompt self-examination; it should not become a claim that we can permanently classify another person’s inner life.

subjects.displayTitle: Beyond self-doubt: capacity discovered through service
subjects.introduction: The portion of some may lie in the palm of a hand, that of others fill a cup, and the cup is no less full for being small. Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel not to weigh the size of the receptacle sets the tone for ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s repeated plea: look not at your own capacity but at the grace of the Lord, which turns a drop into a sea, an atom into a sun, a seed into a laden tree. The earth cannot give itself life, yet it need not bewail its barrenness while sun and rain exist. The Báb reminds His disciples of Abraham against Nimrod and Moses with only a staff. Moses himself, protesting that he could not speak, was given help and a brother to stand with him, a story in which felt inadequacy does not cancel a calling [1]. Confidence of this kind is active: it begins, perseveres, learns by serving, and holds results loosely, since quick success is not always lasting. The journey leads on through the meaning of weakness, the wider discipline of disregarding one’s own capacity, and the spiritual prerequisites that prepare a person to teach.
subjects.arc: Begin with the receiving vessel and the promise of grace, explore images of growing capacity, then move toward initiative, conscientious effort, learning, and patience with results.

order.why: Open with vessels of different sizes receiving their portion of grace.
shortened: The whole duty of man in this Day is to attain that share of the flood of grace which God poureth forth for him. Let none, therefore, consider the largeness or smallness of the receptacle. The portion of some might lie in the palm of a man’s hand, the portion of others might fill a cup, and of others even a gallon-measure.

order.why: Distinguish grace from an allocation based on merit.
shortened: Regarding one's lack of capacity and one's undeserving on the Day of Resurrection, this does not cause one to be shut out from gifts and bounties; for this is not the Day of Justice but the Day of Grace, while justice is allotting to each whatever is his due. Then look thou not at the degree of thy capacity, look thou at the boundless favour of Baha'u'llah; all-encompassing is His bounty, and consummate His grace.

order.why: Shift attention from a mirror’s capacity to the light it receives. Preserve another formulation of the same orientation.
shortened: Day and night I entreat and supplicate to the Kingdom of God and beg for you infinite assistance and confirmation. Do not take into consideration your own aptitudes and capacities, but fix your gaze on the consummate bounty, the divine bestowal and the power of the Holy Spiritâ€"the power that converteth the drop into a sea and the star into a sun.
In this station, merit and capacity are not to be considered; nay rather, the resplendent rays of the Sun of Truth, which have illumined these mirrors, must be taken into account.

order.why: Read the transformation of a drop and an atom as images of bounty.
shortened: Now we must not consider our ability and capacity, nay, rather, we must fix our gaze upon the favors and bounties of God, in these days, Who has made of the drop a sea, and of the atom a sun.

order.why: Add the seed’s growth into a tree.
shortened: Look not at your own capacities, for the divine bestowal can transform a drop into an ocean; it can make a tiny seed a lofty tree.

order.why: Consider the earth receiving sun and rain.
shortened: No capacity is limited when led by the Spirit of God!
The earth of itself has no properties of life, it is barren and dry, until fertilized by the sun and the rain; still the earth need not bewail its own limitations.  May you be given life!

Turn your faces away from the contemplation of your own finite selves and fix your eyes upon the Everlasting Radiance; then will your souls receive in full measure the Divine Power of the Spirit and the Blessings of the Infinite Bounty.

order.why: Connect encouragement amid weakness with joyful service and love.
shortened: One must never consider one's own feebleness, it is the strength of the Holy Spirit of Love, which gives the power to teach. The thought of our own weakness could only bring despair. We must look higher than all earthly thoughts; detach ourselves from every material idea, crave for the things of the spirit; fix our eyes on the everlasting bountiful Mercy of the Almighty, who will fill our souls with the gladness of joyful service to His command 'Love One Another'.

order.why: Read the possibility of guidance arising from someone without formal learning.
shortened: How often has one unlettered soul become the source of guidance for the entire world.
Therefore thou shouldst also trust in God and despite the absence of material means engage in this most profitable trade for thy wealth lies in the Bounty of the Blessed Beauty and in His grace.

order.why: Consider the appeal to look toward grace.
shortened: Look not at thy capacity and ability; nay, look at the grace of thy Lord in these days and at the gift of His Kingdom, the like of which hath never been seen by the eye of existence in former cycles.

order.why: Directly tells a teacher to look to divine bestowal rather than personal power and capacity.
Preserve the concise parallel address to the attracted soul.
shortened: O thou who art attracted to the Fragrances of God!
Consider not thy capacity and merit, nay rather consider the grace of thy Lord, the Clement, the Merciful.

order.why: Read the collective call to regard divine favors.
shortened: Let us not regard our own respective capacities; nay, rather, let us regard forever the favors and bounties of God.

order.why: Pause over the brief assurance of bounty.
shortened: Do ye not look upon your own capacities. Rest ye assured in the bounties of the Blessed Perfection. He shall change the drop into an ocean and the moth into an eagle. He changes the stone into the precious ruby and the scintilla into the world-illuminating sun.

order.why: Connect confidence with actually beginning to speak.
shortened: Therefore do thou not behold thine own capability and ability; nay, during the hour that thou art teaching the Cause of God, turn thy face towards the Kingdom of Abha, beg for divine confirmations and with the utmost confidence and power open thy tongue and speak out boldly all that with which thy heart is inspired.

order.why: Preserve the separately supplied parallel encouragement.
Consider perseverance in the face of opposition.
shortened: None would have the power to deter thee from celebrating His praise, though all men should arise to oppose thee.
Go thou straight on and persevere in His service.

order.why: Complete the linked readings with the Báb’s farewell exhortation and its examples of apparent weakness.
shortened: Heed not your weaknesses and frailty; fix your gaze upon the invincible power of the Lord, your God, the Almighty.

Has He not, in past days, caused Abraham, in spite of His seeming helplessness, to triumph over the forces of Nimrod? Has He not enabled Moses, whose staff was His only companion, to vanquish Pharaoh and his hosts? Has He not established the ascendancy of Jesus, poor and lowly as He was in the eyes of men, over the combined forces of the Jewish people? Has He not subjected the barbarous and militant tribes of Arabia to the holy and transforming discipline of Muhammad, His Prophet?
Arise in His name, put your trust wholly in Him, and be assured of ultimate victory.

order.why: Begin the additional selections with the fullest seed-and-ocean imagery. Read the parallel call to reliance with its supplied wording.
shortened: Look thou not upon thine own capability; the invisible divine confirmations are great and the protection and providence of the Beauty of ABHA is the helper and the assistant. When a drop draws help from the ocean, it is an ocean in itself, and a little seed, through the outpouring of rain, the favor of the sun and the soul-refreshing breeze, will become a tree with the utmost freshness, full of leaves, blossoms and fruits. Therefore, do not consider thy capacity and merit, but rely upon the infinite bounty and trust to His Highness the Almighty.

order.why: Explore the series of transformations from seed to harvest and dust to garden.
shortened: This time I want to send you with a new spirit, a new strength, to enlighten California, and to engage in teaching the Cause in the utmost power. Do not look to yourselves; look to the Bounty of Baha'u'llah; constantly look to His Favor. Do not say you have not capacity; look to the great bounties of Baha'u'llah. One seed becomes a big harvest, a small seed a big tree, one wave an ocean. He makes the dark dust a beautiful garden. This is His power.

order.why: Consider the question of feeling worthy of a task.
shortened: Wherefore, look not on the degree of your capacity, ask not if you are worthy of the task: rest ye your hopes on the help and loving-kindness, the favours and bestowals of Baha'u'llah -- may my soul be offered up for His friends!

order.why: Read the image of sunlight and rain in a remembered conversation.
Retain the brief supplied fragment about infinite grace.
Shift the focus from shortcomings to the purpose of service.
Consider the effects of unproductive self-absorption.
Protect initiative from a disabling focus on deficiencies.
Read the extended account of becoming a channel without claiming personal authorship of results.
shortened: Baha'u'llah and the Master have both urged us repeatedly to disregard our own handicaps and lay our whole reliance upon God. He will come to our help if we only arise and become an active channel for God's grace. Do you think it is the teachers who make converts and change human hearts? No, surely not. They are only pure souls who take the first step, and then let the spirit of Baha'u'llah move them and make use of them. If any one of them should even for a second consider his achievements as due to his own capacities, his work is ended and his fall starts.

order.why: Join confidence with conscientious fulfillment of obligations.
Consider joyful perseverance across different fields of service.
Read the account of becoming more fitted for a task through trying to serve.
Close with patience when growth is slow or not immediately abundant.
shortened: Do not feel discouraged if your labours do not always yield an abundant fruitage. For a quick and rapidly-won success is not always the best and the most lasting. The harder you strive to attain your goal, the greater will be the confirmations of Baha'u'llah, and the more certain you can feel to attain success. Be cheerful, therefore, and exert yourself with full faith and confidence.

questions: What do the images of a vessel, mirror, seed, and drop suggest about capacity as something received and developed?
How can awareness of a limitation become useful preparation rather than a reason never to begin?
What does the account of Moses and Aaron contribute to thinking about help, companionship, and a calling?
How might learning through service combine confidence, conscientious effort, and openness to correction?
What changes when progress is judged by sustained growth rather than immediate or abundant results?

neighbors.invitation: Explore how teaching develops the teacher’s knowledge and character.
Consider the support of shared service.
Read the call to deepen knowledge and meet the needs of another person’s mind.

references.label: 1 · Exodus 4:10–16 (Hebrew–English text, Mechon Mamre)
references.note: Moses names his difficulty with speech, receives a promise of divine help, and is joined by Aaron as a spokesman. Compare this combination of calling, felt inadequacy, and assistance with the exhortations to arise in service. The narrative also invites reflection on companionship and complementary abilities, rather than treating confidence as solitary self-sufficiency.

subjects.displayTitle: Receptivity: the art of offering and listening
subjects.introduction: The cupbearer does not lift the cup until someone is thirsty. Bahá’u’lláh makes that small courtesy the first rule of sharing faith: speech waits on a hearing, and the gems of inner meaning are given only where a quest is already under way. Teaching, so understood, begins as listening. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes changing His whole manner of speaking in the West because the proofs that moved an Eastern audience would not have been heard at all, and He tells of a boy who sent a learned skeptic away to find seeing eyes,. Food too rich for a child causes rejection; a physician diagnoses before prescribing; the time for some truths has not yet come. Confucius likewise lifts one corner of a subject and waits for the learner to find the other three [1]. And yet readiness is not ours to judge, every door should be open, and a friendship that never becomes shared belief is still a friendship. The questions that remain lead on to the differences in human capacity, to the universal capacity for recognising truth that underlies them, and to the methods of teaching.
subjects.arc: Begin with attentive offering, examine adaptation and timing, then consider honest explanation, inclusive community, the limits of judging readiness, and friendship without insistence.

order.why: Open with the cupbearer who waits for a seeker.
Read the prayer responding to thirst, hunger, and a need for knowledge.
shortened: Verily Thy lovers thirst, O my Lord; lead them to the wellspring of bounty and grace. Verily, they hunger; send down unto them Thy heavenly table. Verily, they are naked; robe them in the garments of learning and knowledge.

order.why: Connect the offering of inner meanings with an observed quest.
shortened: Until you find thirst, bestow not the Kawthar of divine knowledge; until you observe the quest, grant not the gems of inner meanings.

order.why: Consider the reported encounter in which a listener later returns.
Read the extended explanation of adapting speech to different audiences.
shortened: During this journey through Europe and America, whatever was spoken was in consideration of the capacity, inclination, and attitude of the inhabitants and nations, even to the point that teaching was according to their taste and temperament. It was observed that if proofs and arguments were presented according to the principles of teaching in the East, and if truths and meanings were discussed, it would have absolutely no effect on the listeners. Therefore, the manner and method of teaching was changed. The presentation became focused on issues, teachings, and the foundation of the Cause of God, for the listeners would grasp the meaning and understand, whereas if it were not done in this way, they would not listen at all.
One must consider the capacity of the hearers and speak accordingly. As Rumi says:"To his little child the father speaks in baby-talk,Though his mind may comprehend the geometry of the world."

order.why: Notice the reported influence of upheaval on receptivity.
shortened: Due to severe upheavals, souls have acquired an extraordinary receptivity - when these upheavals are forgotten, this receptivity will not remain.

order.why: Instructs teachers to respond promptly when receptivity and favorable conditions appear in a locality.
Complete the linked readings with the vivid, but limited, analogy of different materials.
Read forbearance and regard for understanding as guiding qualities.
shortened: It behooveth the people of God to be forbearing. They should impart the Word of God according to the hearer’s particular measure of understanding and capacity, that perchance the children of men may be roused from heedlessness and set their faces towards this Horizon which is immeasurably exalted above every horizon.

order.why: Distinguish what can be said from what is timely and suitable.
shortened: How many meanings are there that words cannot contain! How many of them have no expression and have been given neither statement nor allusion! And how many of them cannot be uttered because their time hath not come, as it hath been said: "Not all that is known can be disclosed, nor is the time ripe for all that can be disclosed, nor are the people capable of hearing all for which the time is ripe." And there are those whose mention dependeth upon knowledge of the Dawning-Places wherein We have expounded the sciences and revealed what was hidden.

order.why: Examine the food and physician analogies with the supplied references intact.
shortened: Follow thou the way of thy Lord, and say not that which the ears cannot bear to hear, for such speech is like luscious food given to small children. However palatable, rare and rich the food may be, it cannot be assimilated by the digestive organs of a suckling child. Therefore unto every one who hath a right, let his settled measure be given.

"Not everything that a man knoweth can be disclosed, nor can everything that he can disclose be regarded as timely, nor can every timely utterance be considered as suited to the capacity of those who hear it."
First diagnose the disease and identify the malady, then prescribe the remedy, for such is the perfect method of the skillful physician.

order.why: Consider moderation and the learner’s subsequent discovery.
shortened: And He said: "Blessed is he who giveth the people to drink from the sea of the utterance of the All-Merciful without speaking a word that would cause rejection and objection." Indeed, forbearance is most beloved. Any soul who shows the slightest acceptance will later comprehend most matters himself, but if at first a word is expressed that is beyond his capacity, he will not bear it and will arise in opposition.

order.why: Read the historical example of beginning from scriptures an audience already accepts.
shortened: Second, that it is most clear that speech is measured according to the capacity of minds. That Epistle was written because certain of the kindred of the Primal Point---may the spirit of all else save Him be sacrificed unto Him---were in doubt concerning some matters, and had not yet passed from the Furqan unto the Bayan. Therefore, for the people of the Furqan, proofs were adduced from Qur'anic verses, lest they be troubled, for they had not yet believed in the Bayan so that mention might be made to them of the wondrous verses of the Bayan.

order.why: Place deeds before speech in cultivating interest.
Begin the additional selections with the responsibility placed on the speaker.
Examine gradual disclosure through the example of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá.
shortened: It was He, our beloved 'Abdu'l-Baha, our true and shining Exemplar, who with infinite tact and patience, whether in His public utterances or in private converse, adapted the presentation of the fundamentals of the Cause to the varying capacities and the spiritual receptiveness of His hearers. He never hesitated, however, to tear the veil asunder and reveal to the spiritually ripened those challenging verities that set forth in its true light the relationship of this Supreme Revelation with the Dispensations of the past.

order.why: Consider why no single rule fits every teacher and hearer.
shortened: Shoghi Effendi feels that he can lay down no rule as to when one should introduce the names of the Bab, Baha'u'llah and 'Abdu'l-Baha in one's teaching. Much depends on the temperament and aptitude both of the teacher and the one taught.... We must look to the example of the Master and follow our "Inner Light", adapting our message as best we can to the capacity and "ripeness" of the one we are seeking to teach....

order.why: Read the differentiated approaches together with the duty eventually to explain the whole message.
shortened: Every inquirer has to be approached from his own angle. Those who are essentially of the mystic type should first be given those teachings of the Cause which emphasize the nature and value of spiritual realities; while those who are practically minded and of a positive type are naturally more ready and inclined to accept the social aspect of the Teachings. But of course, gradually the entire Message, in all its aspects and with the full implications it entails, should be explained to the newcomer. For to be a believer means to accept the Cause in its wholeness, and not to adhere to some of its teachings.

order.why: Consider the choice of direct and indirect approaches.
Read the forceful warning about overwhelming another person, retaining its provisional status.
shortened: It behooveth the wayfarer to guard this knowledge deposited in the receptacles of enlightened hearts by God the creator of mankind, to protect it as his eyes, and to conceal it in his breast. Were he to reveal one letter of these secrets other than to those who are worthy, he shall have perpetuated three serious crimes. The first is betrayal inasmuch as he hath betrayed God by exposing His mysteries to those unsuited to hear them. The second is injustice inasmuch as he conferred this station upon one who doth not deserve it, and weighed him down with an unbearable load he cannot carry.

The third is murder because he misled this wretched one and killed him by killing his faith, inasmuch as he was unable to comprehend this divine knowledge, his feet slipped from whence he had progressed in the Cause of his Origin and Return.

order.why: Examine the need for scholarship responsive to contemporary questions.
Consider the call to present deeper teachings intelligently.
Read the encouragement to enter intellectual conversations with confidence.
Keep the explicit rejection of class prejudice beside the interest in ability.
Read the call for wise and eloquent teachers among people of prominence.
Consider the historical appeal for a wider range of accomplishments within the community.
Distinguish attracting new capacities from developing existing ones.
Explore expertise as a contribution to social problems.
Consider the community’s responsibility for patient and loving welcome.
Recognize the value of friendship even without conversion.
Read the process of growing participation and maturity.
Clarify what a person should know when declaring belief.
Join gentleness at entry with the expectation of a life shaped by the teachings.
Read the example requiring disclosure of a religious obligation before joining.
Consider spiritual responsibility expressed without shocks or pressure.
Examine tact in relation to different people and circumstances.
Read the further counsel against dogmatism about secondary practices.
Challenge the assumption that apparent lack of readiness tells the whole story.
Protect the opportunity to hear from being withheld through neglect.
Read the prayer to meet those who are ready.
Preserve its separately supplied daily formulation.
Connect deep study and meditation with thoughtful action.
shortened: The beloved Guardian has stressed over and over again, that to effectively teach the Faith, the individual must study deeply, the Divine Word, imbibe Its life-giving waters, and feast upon Its glorious teachings. He should then meditate on the import of the Word, and finding its spiritual depths, pray for guidance and assistance. But most important, after prayer is action. After one has prayed and meditated, he must arise, relying fully on the guidance and confirmation of Baha'u'llah, to teach His Faith.

order.why: Close with friendship and the clear instruction not to insist.

questions: What might attentive listening reveal that a prepared explanation alone would miss?
How can a speaker adapt language and timing while remaining honest about the full implications of a belief?
What does the Analects contribute to understanding the learner’s own active role?
How should the warning against judging readiness be held together with the instruction not to insist on teaching someone who is uninterested?
What would a community need to learn in order to welcome people of varied backgrounds and abilities without class prejudice?
How might friendship retain its value when a religious conversation does not lead to shared belief?

neighbors.invitation: Consider whether an apparent shortage of receptive people may also reveal a shortage of attentive cupbearers.
Explore growing in ability through the act of serving.
Connect the influence of words with good deeds and character.

references.label: 1 · Confucius, Analects 7.8 (Internet Classics Archive)
references.note: In Book 7, the saying about presenting one corner of a subject connects instruction with eagerness to understand and the learner’s ability to infer the remaining corners. Compare this emphasis on active participation with the images of thirst and suitable nourishment. The teaching situations differ, but both prompt questions about what a teacher can offer and what a learner must discover through their own effort.
